questions.question: In 1836, ________ became the Governor General of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earl of Auckland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **George Eden, 1st Earl of Auckland**, served as the Governor-General of India from 1836 to 1842.
 
• He is most known for his involvement in the **First Anglo-Afghan War (1839-1842)**, which ultimately ended in disaster for the British.
 
• Earl of Auckland succeeded Lord William Bentinck as the Governor-General.
 
• During his tenure, he implemented several administrative reforms and efforts to improve education and public works.
 
• He was eventually succeeded by Lord Ellenborough in 1842 following the failure in Afghanistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Anglo-Afghan War**

 
 
• The war was fought between the British East India Company and the Emirate of Afghanistan from 1839 to 1842.
 
• The conflict was initiated by the British to install a puppet regime in Afghanistan and counter Russian influence in the region.
 
• The war ended in a catastrophic retreat for the British, famously known as the Retreat from Kabul in 1842.
 
• It resulted in significant loss of life and resources for the British forces.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Reforms**
 
 
• Earl of Auckland focused on improving the administrative efficiency of the British Indian government.
 
• He supported the expansion of the educational system in India, including the establishment of schools and colleges.
 
• His tenure also saw the improvement of public works, such as the construction of roads and irrigation projects.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**
 
 
• Despite the failure in Afghanistan, Earl of Auckland's efforts in education and public works left a lasting impact.
 
• His tenure is often remembered for its administrative and infrastructural improvements in British India.
 
• He was later commemorated in various namesakes, including the Auckland Islands in the Southern Ocean.

questions.question: The GV Raja Memorial Trophy, Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee Trophy and Santosh Trophy are related to which of the following sports in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Football**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The GV Raja Memorial Trophy is an annual football tournament held in Kerala, India, named after the sports promoter, Col. Godavarma Raja.
 
• The Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee Trophy is associated with football tournaments at the university level in India, aimed at promoting the sport among students.
 
• The Santosh Trophy is one of the most prestigious football tournaments in India, organized by the All India Football Federation (AIFF), and serves as the national championship for state teams.
 
• These tournaments have played a significant role in the development and promotion of football at various levels, from grassroots to professional, within the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All India Football Federation (AIFF)**

 
 
• The AIFF is the governing body of football in India and is responsible for organizing national tournaments such as the Santosh Trophy, I-League, and Indian Super League (ISL).
 
• It was founded in 1937 and is affiliated with the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).
 
 
 
• **Indian Super League (ISL)**
 
 
• The ISL is one of the top professional football leagues in India, established in 2013 to promote football and increase its popularity.
 
• The league operates with a franchise-based model, similar to the Indian Premier League (IPL) in cricket.
 
 
 
• **I-League**
 
 
• The I-League is another prominent professional football league in India, running parallel to the ISL.
 
• It was established in 2007 as the top-tier football league in the country, aimed at improving the standard of Indian football.
 
 
 
• **National Football Team**
 
 
• India's national football team is managed by the AIFF and competes in various international tournaments, including the AFC Asian Cup and FIFA World Cup qualifiers.
 
• Sunil Chhetri, one of India's most famous footballers, has been a key player for the national team, contributing significantly to its success.

questions.question: A disease like COVID-19 is a kind of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zoonotic disease**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which is believed to have originated in bats and potentially transmitted to humans through an intermediate host.
 
• Zoonotic diseases are infections that are transmitted from animals to humans. Examples include Ebola, Rabies, and Avian Influenza.
 
• Such diseases can spread through direct contact with animals, by consuming contaminated food or water, or via vectors like mosquitoes.
 
• Zoonotic diseases pose significant challenges to public health due to their potential for widespread outbreaks and pandemics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:**

 
 
• **Zoonosis:** An infectious disease that has jumped from a non-human animal to humans.
 
• **Vector:** An organism, typically a biting insect or tick, that transmits a disease or parasite from one animal or plant to another.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Zoonotic Diseases:**
 
 
• **Ebola:** Transmitted to humans through contact with blood, secretions, organs, or other bodily fluids of infected animals.
 
• **Rabies:** A viral disease that causes inflammation of the brain in humans and other mammals.
 
• **Avian Influenza:** Commonly known as bird flu, it is a viral infection that can infect not only birds but also humans and other animals.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 Transmission:**
 
 
• The primary mode of transmission is through respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or talks.
 
• It can also spread by touching surfaces contaminated with the virus and then touching the face.
 
 
 
• **Public Health Measures:**
 
 
• Preventive measures include wearing masks, practicing hand hygiene, and maintaining physical distance.
 
• Controlling zoonotic diseases involves monitoring animal health, regulating wildlife trade, and ensuring food safety.

questions.question: In February 2023, who was appointed as the new Governor of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shiv Pratap Shukla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shiv Pratap Shukla was appointed as the Governor of Himachal Pradesh in February 2023.
 
• He succeeded Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, the former Governor of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• Shukla has served as a Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha representing the state of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• He is a senior leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and has held various key positions in the party and government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of a Governor**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of each of the states in India.
 
• They are appointed by the President of India for a term of five years.
 
• The Governor acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• The Governor has the power to summon, prorogue, and dissolve the state legislature.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh is located in the northern part of India.
 
• The state is known for its scenic beauty, including the Himalayan mountains.
 
• It was granted statehood on 25th January 1971.
 
• The capital of Himachal Pradesh is Shimla, and its largest city is also Shimla.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**
 
 
• The BJP is one of the two major political parties in India, along with the Indian National Congress.
 
• It was founded in 1980 by members of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh.
 
• The party advocates for a policy of integral humanism, which was first formulated by Deendayal Upadhyaya.
 
• The BJP has been the ruling party in India since 2014 under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

questions.question: Who is properly known as the 'Grand Old Lady' of the Independence Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aruna Asaf Ali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Aruna Asaf Ali is popularly known as the 'Grand Old Lady' of the Indian Independence Movement due to her significant contribution to India's struggle for freedom.
 
• She is best remembered for hoisting the Indian National Congress flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, during the Quit India Movement in 1942.
 
• Aruna Asaf Ali played a crucial role in organizing protests, strikes, and other activities against British rule, demonstrating her unwavering dedication to India's independence.
 
• She was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1997 posthumously for her invaluable contributions to the nation.
 
• She was also the first elected Mayor of Delhi, representing her leadership and influence in post-independence India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quit India Movement:**

 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• It was a mass protest demanding "Do or Die" for independence.
 
• Aruna Asaf Ali's hoisting of the flag became a symbol of defiance against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Ratna:**
 
 
• India's highest civilian award, instituted in 1954.
 
• Awarded for exceptional service in the highest order in any field of human endeavor.
 
• Recipients include prominent figures such as C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, and Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress:**
 
 
• Founded in 1885, played a pivotal role in India's independence movement.
 
• Leaders like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel were its prominent members.
 
• Organized major movements like Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, and Quit India Movement.
 
 
 
• **Role of Women in Independence Movement:**
 
 
• Women leaders like Sarojini Naidu, Kasturba Gandhi, and Kamala Nehru played significant roles.
 
• They participated in protests, boycotts, and were also imprisoned.
 
• Their involvement showcased the inclusive nature of the independence struggle.

questions.question: Which of the following river valleys is NOT known for coal deposits in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satluj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Satluj River is not known for coal deposits, unlike other river valleys listed in the options.
 
• Coal deposits are primarily found in the river valleys of the Mahanadi, Godavari, and Son rivers in India.
 
• Major coalfields in the Mahanadi Valley include Talcher and Ib Valley.
 
• Godavari Valley is known for its Singareni and Kothagudem coalfields.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coal Distribution in India:**

 
 
• India has significant coal reserves, primarily located in the eastern and central parts of the country.
 
• The largest reserves are found in Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Types of Coal:**
 
 
• Anthracite: The highest grade of coal with the highest carbon content.
 
• Bituminous: Most common type, used for electricity generation and steel production.
 
• Sub-bituminous: Lower carbon content, used mainly for electricity generation.
 
• Lignite: Lowest grade, often used for electricity generation in power plants.
 
 
 
• **Coal Mining Methods:**
 
 
• Open-pit mining: Extracting coal from the surface.
 
• Underground mining: Extracting coal from deep below the earth's surface.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Coal mining and usage contribute to air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Efforts are being made to reduce the environmental impact through cleaner coal technologies.

questions.question: In 2023, which repository is proposed to be set up in a digital epigraphy museum, with digitisation of one lakh ancient inscriptions in the first stage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharat Shared Repository of Inscriptions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bharat Shared Repository of Inscriptions (BSRI) is an initiative aimed at digitising ancient inscriptions across India.
 
• In its first phase, the project targets the digitisation of one lakh ancient inscriptions.
 
• The repository will be part of a digital epigraphy museum to preserve and share ancient Indian heritage.
 
• This initiative will help in the conservation, study, and promotion of India's rich epigraphical heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Epigraphy**

 
 
• Epigraphy is the study and interpretation of ancient inscriptions engraved on various materials like stone, metal, or pottery.
 
• It provides valuable insights into the language, culture, and history of ancient civilizations.
 
• Epigraphical records are primary historical sources that help in understanding the chronology and events of the past.
 
 
 
• **Digitisation of Inscriptions**
 
 
• Digitisation involves converting physical inscriptions into digital formats to ensure their preservation and accessibility.
 
• It helps in preventing the loss of historical data due to physical degradation over time.
 
• Digital repositories allow researchers and the public to access these inscriptions from anywhere in the world.
 
 
 
• **National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities**
 
 
• The National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities was launched by the Government of India to document and preserve India's heritage.
 
• It aims to create a comprehensive database of monuments and antiquities across the country.
 
• This mission plays a crucial role in protecting and promoting India's cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Digital Museums**
 
 
• Digital museums use technology to display and interpret cultural and historical artifacts.
 
• They provide an immersive experience to visitors through interactive exhibits and virtual tours.
 
• Digital museums help in reaching a wider audience and making heritage accessible to all.

questions.question: The amount of dissolved oxygen in water becomes lowest at what time of the day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In the dawn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The amount of dissolved oxygen in water is typically lowest just before dawn due to the lack of photosynthesis during the night.
 
• Photosynthesis by aquatic plants and algae ceases at night, leading to the consumption of oxygen by respiration without replenishment.
 
• Respiration by aquatic organisms continues throughout the night, further depleting oxygen levels.
 
• Warmer water temperatures at night can also reduce the solubility of oxygen in water.
 
• This phenomenon is particularly significant in eutrophic water bodies with high levels of organic matter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dissolved Oxygen (DO):**

 
 
• Dissolved oxygen refers to the amount of oxygen that is present in water, which is crucial for the survival of aquatic life.
 
• DO levels are influenced by temperature, salinity, and the presence of photosynthetic organisms.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants and some other organisms use sunlight to synthesize foods with the help of chlorophyll.
 
• During photosynthesis, oxygen is produced as a byproduct.
 
 
 
• **Respiration:**
 
 
• Respiration is the process of breaking down food to release energy, which consumes oxygen and produces carbon dioxide.
 
• Both aquatic plants and animals undergo respiration.
 
 
 
• **Eutrophication:**
 
 
• Eutrophication is the process by which a body of water becomes overly enriched with minerals and nutrients, leading to excessive growth of algae.
 
• This can result in oxygen depletion in water bodies.
 
 
 
• **Water Temperature:**
 
 
• Water temperature plays a critical role in determining the solubility of oxygen.
 
• Higher temperatures reduce the solubility of oxygen in water.

questions.question: The percentage of sunlight energy absorbed by the green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem is about ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Only about **1%** of the sunlight energy that reaches the surface of the Earth is absorbed by green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem.
 
• This small fraction is due to the limitations in the efficiency of photosynthesis and the availability of light that plants can utilize.
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
 
• Most of the sunlight is either reflected by the plant leaves or absorbed as heat, with only a small fraction being used for photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis Process**

 
 
• Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells, where chlorophyll captures light energy.
 
• The process converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, using the captured light energy.
 
• It is a crucial process for the survival of plants and the production of oxygen for other living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Energy Flow in Ecosystems**
 
 
• Energy flow in ecosystems begins with the absorption of sunlight by producers (green plants).
 
• Only a small fraction of the total sunlight is converted into chemical energy by plants, and this energy is passed through the food chain.
 
• At each trophic level, energy is lost as heat, leading to a decrease in the amount of energy available to higher trophic levels.
 
 
 
• **Light Absorption in Plants**
 
 
• Plant leaves contain pigments like chlorophyll that absorb light primarily in the blue and red wavelengths.
 
• Green light is mostly reflected, which is why plants appear green to our eyes.
 
• The efficiency of light absorption and conversion to chemical energy is limited by various factors, including the intensity and duration of light.
 
 
 
• **Global Primary Production**
 
 
• Primary production is the creation of organic compounds from atmospheric or aquatic carbon dioxide, mainly through photosynthesis.
 
• Terrestrial primary production is a key component of the global carbon cycle, influencing climate and ecosystem dynamics.
 
• The efficiency of primary production varies among different ecosystems and is influenced by factors such as climate, nutrient availability, and plant species.

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel 'Life and Death of Sambhaji' published in the year 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Medha Deshmukh Bhaskaran**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The novel 'Life and Death of Sambhaji' was authored by **Medha Deshmukh Bhaskaran**.
 
• The book was published in the year **2021**.
 
• Medha Deshmukh Bhaskaran is known for her detailed and well-researched historical novels.
 
• The novel focuses on the life and times of **Sambhaji Maharaj**, the second Chhatrapati of the Maratha Empire.
 
• The book provides a comprehensive account of Sambhaji Maharaj's contributions and struggles during his reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sambhaji Maharaj**

 
 
• He was the eldest son of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and succeeded him as the ruler of the Maratha Empire.
 
• Sambhaji Maharaj's reign lasted from 1681 to 1689.
 
• He faced numerous challenges, including conflicts with the Mughal Empire, Portuguese, and Siddis.
 
• He is remembered for his valor, administrative skills, and dedication to preserving the Maratha sovereignty.
 
 
 
• **Historical Novels**
 
 
• These are novels set in a past time period, often incorporating real historical events and characters.
 
• They aim to provide readers with a deeper understanding of historical events through the lens of fictional narratives.
 
• Authors often conduct extensive research to ensure historical accuracy and authenticity in their storytelling.
 
• Historical novels can cover various genres, including romance, adventure, and drama, set against historical backdrops.
 
 
 
• **Medha Deshmukh Bhaskaran**
 
 
• She is a well-regarded author in the field of historical fiction.
 
• Her works are known for their meticulous research and engaging narrative style.
 
• In addition to 'Life and Death of Sambhaji,' she has written other notable works, contributing significantly to Indian historical literature.
 
• Her books often focus on prominent figures and events in Indian history, offering readers an immersive experience.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of Buddhist population in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Census 2011, Sikkim has the highest percentage of Buddhist population among all states in India.
 
• Approximately 27.39% of the population in Sikkim follows Buddhism.
 
• Buddhism is one of the major religions practiced in Sikkim, alongside Hinduism and Christianity.
 
• The state is known for its many Buddhist monasteries, such as the Rumtek Monastery and Tashiding Monastery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011:**

 
 
• The Census 2011 is the 15th National census survey conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on the population size, distribution, and various demographic attributes of India's population.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism in India:**
 
 
• Buddhism originated in India around the 5th century BCE with the teachings of Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha.
 
• It spread across Asia and has a significant following in countries like Tibet, Myanmar, Thailand, and Japan.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Monasteries in Sikkim:**
 
 
• Rumtek Monastery is one of the largest and most significant monasteries in Sikkim, serving as the headquarters of the Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism.
 
• Tashiding Monastery is another important religious site, known for its annual Bumchu Festival.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Sikkim's culture is heavily influenced by Buddhism, reflected in its festivals, architecture, and daily life.
 
• The state celebrates various Buddhist festivals like Losar, Saga Dawa, and Lhabab Duchen with great fervor.

questions.question: As per Article 163 of the Constitution of India, any advice tendered by Ministers to the _______ shall not be inquired into in any court.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 163 of the Constitution of India pertains to the Council of Ministers advising the Governor of a state.
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state, and the real executive authority lies with the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• According to Article 163(3), the question of whether any, and if so what, advice was tendered by Ministers to the Governor shall not be inquired into in any court.
 
• This provision is meant to preserve the confidentiality of the advice given by the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
 
• The Governor acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers except in cases where he/she is required to act in his/her discretion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role**

 
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• The Governor's powers include legislative powers, executive powers, financial powers, and judicial powers.
 
• The Governor has the power to summon, prorogue, and dissolve the state legislature.
 
• In certain situations, the Governor can act independently, such as in the appointment of the Chief Minister when there is no clear majority.
 
 
 
• **Council of Ministers**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers, headed by the Chief Minister, aids and advises the Governor in the exercise of his/her functions.
 
• It is collectively responsible to the legislative assembly of the state.
 
• The Council of Ministers is instrumental in policy formulation and administration of the state.
 
 
 
• **Discretionary Powers of the Governor**
 
 
• Discretionary powers are exercised by the Governor without the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• These powers include reserving a bill for the President's consideration, recommending President's Rule, and seeking information from the Chief Minister regarding the legislative and administrative matters of the state.
 
• The Governor also has the discretion to appoint the Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority in the legislative assembly.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Immunity**
 
 
• Article 163(3) ensures judicial immunity to the advice given by the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
 
• This immunity is designed to maintain the confidentiality and integrity of the executive advice process.

questions.question: Chitti Babu is a famous player of which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Veena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chitti Babu was a renowned Veena player from India, recognized for his exceptional skill and contribution to Carnatic music.
 
• He started learning the Veena at a very young age and was tutored by Emani Sankara Sastry, a legendary veena player.
 
• Chitti Babu's playing style was noted for its melodic beauty, technical proficiency, and deep emotional expression.
 
• He performed extensively in India and internationally, popularizing the Veena and Carnatic music across the globe.
 
• Chitti Babu received numerous awards and honors, including the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and Kalaimamani Award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Veena**

 
 
• The Veena is a traditional Indian string instrument used primarily in Carnatic classical music.
 
• It consists of a large resonating body, a long neck, and seven strings, with four main playing strings and three drone strings.
 
• The instrument is known for its deep, resonant sound and is played using a combination of plucking and sliding techniques.
 
• The Veena has a history dating back to ancient times and is considered one of the oldest musical instruments in India.
 
• It is often associated with the goddess Saraswati, the Hindu deity of knowledge, music, and arts.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music**
 
 
• Carnatic music is a system of classical music associated with the southern part of India.
 
• It is known for its intricate and complex compositions, known as kritis, which are often devotional in nature.
 
• The music emphasizes vocal performance, but instruments like the Veena, Mridangam, and Violin are also integral.
 
• Carnatic music is characterized by its use of ragas (melodic scales) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• Training and performance in Carnatic music require years of rigorous practice and dedication.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• This is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists for their outstanding contribution to the performing arts.
 
• The award is presented by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• It was instituted in 1952 and includes a citation, a plaque, and a cash prize.
 
• Recipients are chosen for their excellence in the fields of music, dance, and drama.
 
 
 
• **Kalaimamani Award**
 
 
• The Kalaimamani Award is a prestigious award given by the Tamil Nadu government to artists in the fields of art and literature.
 
• It was instituted in 1954 and is presented annually by the Tamil Nadu Eyal Isai Nataka Manram (Tamil Nadu State Academy).
 
• The award recognizes contributions to Tamil culture and includes a medal and a citation.
 
• It is one of the highest honors for artists in the state of Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Which of the following microfinance units were established in India at the time of independence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rural Cooperatives**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rural Cooperatives were one of the earliest forms of microfinance institutions established in India.
 
• They were set up to provide credit and financial services to rural and agricultural sectors.
 
• The aim was to eliminate the exploitation by moneylenders and to provide farmers with access to necessary financial resources.
 
• These cooperatives played a crucial role in the development and upliftment of rural areas post-independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grameen Model Banks**

 
 
• This model was popularized by Muhammad Yunus in Bangladesh and is not originally from India.
 
• It focuses on group-based lending and has been adapted in various parts of the world.
 
 
 
• **Joint Liability Groups (JLGs)**
 
 
• Introduced much later as a microfinance model to provide loans based on group guarantees.
 
• They are aimed at ensuring credit access to small farmers and rural entrepreneurs.
 
 
 
• **Self Help Groups (SHGs)**
 
 
• These were introduced in India in the 1980s and gained popularity in the 1990s.
 
• SHGs are small groups of people who come together to save and lend to each other.
 
• They are often linked with banks for larger financial support.
 
 
 
• **Cooperative Societies Act**
 
 
• In India, the first Cooperative Societies Act was passed in 1904.
 
• This act laid the foundation for the cooperative movement in India.
 
• The act aimed at providing a legal framework for cooperative societies.

questions.question: Which of the following harvest and cultural festivals is celebrated by the Tamil community every year in January?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pongal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pongal is a major harvest festival celebrated by the Tamil community in the month of January every year.
 
• The festival lasts for four days, usually from January 14th to January 17th, marking the Tamil New Year.
 
• It is named after the Tamil word "Pongal," meaning "to boil," and is celebrated with the boiling of the first rice of the season.
 
• The festival is dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and signifies the end of the winter solstice and the start of the sun's six-month-long journey northwards.
 
• Pongal is celebrated with traditional rituals, including cooking a special dish called "Pongal" and offering it to the deities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhogi Pongal**

 
 
• The first day of Pongal is called Bhogi Pongal and is dedicated to Lord Indra, the god of rain.
 
• On this day, old and unwanted items are burned in a bonfire to mark the end of the old and the beginning of the new.
 
 
 
• **Surya Pongal**
 
 
• The second day, Surya Pongal, is dedicated to the Sun God and is the main day of the festival.
 
• People prepare a dish of rice, milk, and jaggery and offer it to the Sun God as a gesture of gratitude.
 
 
 
• **Mattu Pongal**
 
 
• The third day, Mattu Pongal, is dedicated to cattle (Mattu) which are considered essential for farming in Tamil culture.
 
• Cattle are decorated and worshipped, and farmers express their gratitude to them for their hard work throughout the year.
 
 
 
• **Kanum Pongal**
 
 
• The fourth day, Kanum Pongal, is a day for socializing and relaxation.
 
• Families visit relatives and friends, and various cultural events and games are organized.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Kolam**
 
 
• During Pongal, homes are decorated with beautiful Kolam (rangoli) designs made using rice flour.
 
• Kolam is believed to bring prosperity and happiness and is an integral part of the Pongal celebrations.

questions.question: The temperature of -273.15°C is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**absolute zero temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Absolute zero temperature is defined as -273.15°C or 0 Kelvin (K).
 
• At absolute zero, the entropy of a perfect crystal is exactly zero, according to the Third Law of Thermodynamics.
 
• Absolute zero is the theoretical point where particles have minimum thermal motion.
 
• It represents the lowest limit of the thermodynamic temperature scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kelvin Scale**

 
 
• The Kelvin scale is the SI unit of temperature measurement.
 
• It starts from absolute zero, where 0 K is equal to -273.15°C.
 
• 1 Kelvin is equivalent to 1°C in terms of the temperature interval.
 
 
 
• **Third Law of Thermodynamics**
 
 
• States that as the temperature approaches absolute zero, the entropy of a system approaches a constant minimum.
 
• This law implies that it is impossible to reach absolute zero through any finite number of processes.
 
 
 
• **Absolute Zero in Practice**
 
 
• Absolute zero cannot be achieved experimentally, but scientists can get very close to it.
 
• Techniques like laser cooling and magnetic evaporative cooling are used to reach temperatures near absolute zero.
 
 
 
• **Implications of Absolute Zero**
 
 
• At absolute zero, molecular motion ceases, and a system reaches its ground state.
 
• Understanding absolute zero helps in the study of quantum mechanics and superconductivity.

questions.question: What does Age Structure represent?

options.text: The number of females per 100 males in a given area at a specified time period
The number of females per 1000 males in a given area at a specified time period
The proportion of persons in different age groups relative to the total population
A measure comparing the portion of a population composed of dependents with the portion that is in the working age group

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The proportion of persons in different age groups relative to the total population**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Age structure represents the distribution of various age groups within a population.
 
• It is a critical demographic tool used to understand the age composition of a population.
 
• Age structure helps in planning and policy-making, particularly in areas such as education, healthcare, and employment.
 
• Analyzing age structure can reveal trends such as aging populations or youth bulges, which have significant socio-economic implications.
 
• It is typically illustrated through population pyramids, which graphically represent the age and sex distribution of a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Pyramid**

 
 
• A graphical representation that shows the distribution of various age groups in a population, typically separated by sex.
 
• It can indicate population growth trends, with wider bases showing younger populations and narrower bases indicating older populations.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Transition**
 
 
• A model that describes population change over time, transitioning from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates.
 
• It typically involves four stages: pre-industrial, transitional, industrial, and post-industrial.
 
 
 
• **Dependency Ratio**
 
 
• A measure comparing the portion of a population composed of dependents (young and old) with the portion that is in the working age group.
 
• A high dependency ratio indicates that the working population is supporting a larger proportion of non-working individuals.
 
 
 
• **Median Age**
 
 
• The age that divides a population into two numerically equal groups, with half the people younger and half older than that age.
 
• It is an indicator of the overall age distribution of a population.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy**
 
 
• The average number of years a person is expected to live based on current mortality rates.
 
• It is a key indicator of the overall health and well-being of a population.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: In which of the following cities was the first successful textile mill established in India in the year 1854?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first successful textile mill in India was established in Bombay (now Mumbai) in 1854.
 
• It was set up by Cowasji Nanabhai Davar and was named Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company.
 
• This marked the beginning of the cotton textile industry in India.
 
• Bombay rapidly became the center of textile production in India, contributing significantly to the city’s economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Textile Industry in India:**

 
 
• The textile industry is one of the largest industries in India, both in terms of production and employment.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in the Indian economy, contributing about 2.3% to the GDP and 13% to industrial production.
 
• India is one of the largest producers and exporters of textiles and garments in the world.
 
• The industry is labor-intensive and employs around 45 million people directly and 60 million people indirectly.
 
 
 
• **Cotton Textile Industry:**
 
 
• Cotton textiles were among the first industries to develop in India during the British colonial period.
 
• It remains a major segment of the Indian textile industry, with states like Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and West Bengal being major producers.
 
• Modernization and expansion in the cotton textile industry have led to increased productivity and quality.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Industrialization:**
 
 
• The establishment of textile mills played a crucial role in the industrialization of India.
 
• It led to urbanization and economic development in several regions, particularly in Bombay.
 
• Industrialization also brought about significant social changes, including the rise of a new working class and changes in labor practices.
 
 
 
• **Modern Textile Industry:**
 
 
• Today's textile industry in India is highly diversified, producing a wide range of products from traditional handloom fabrics to modern synthetic textiles.
 
• It continues to be a major contributor to India's export economy, with key markets in the USA, European Union, and Middle East.
 
• Government initiatives like the Textile Policy aim to support and promote the growth and modernization of the textile sector.

questions.question: In which year was the first Senior Women's National Football Championship held in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first Senior Women's National Football Championship was held in India in **1992**.
 
• This championship was introduced to promote women's football in the country.
 
• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) organized the tournament.
 
• The inaugural tournament witnessed participation from various states across India.
 
• It has since become an annual event, fostering the growth of women's football nationwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All India Football Federation (AIFF)**

 
 
• AIFF is the governing body for football in India.
 
• It was founded in 1937 and is affiliated with FIFA, the global governing body for football.
 
• AIFF is responsible for organizing national competitions and promoting football at all levels.
 
• It oversees both men's and women's football activities in India.
 
 
 
• **Growth of Women's Football in India**
 
 
• Women's football in India has gained significant momentum over the past few decades.
 
• Various national and regional tournaments are held to encourage participation.
 
• The Indian Women's National Football Team has competed in several international tournaments.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to improve infrastructure and training facilities for women footballers.
 
 
 
• **Importance of National Championships**
 
 
• National championships provide a platform for players to showcase their talent.
 
• They help in identifying and nurturing future stars of the sport.
 
• Such tournaments promote a competitive spirit and improve the overall standard of the game.
 
• They also help in building a strong foundation for the national teams.
 
 
 
• **Women's Football Initiatives by AIFF**
 
 
• AIFF has launched several initiatives to boost women's football.
 
• These include grassroots programs, coaching camps, and talent scouting missions.
 
• AIFF also collaborates with international bodies for technical support and training.
 
• There is a focus on increasing participation at the school and college levels.

questions.question: The last Chalukyan King, defeated by the Rashtrakuta King Dantidurga, was ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirtivarman II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kirtivarman II was the last ruler of the Chalukya dynasty who reigned in the Deccan region.
 
• He was defeated by Dantidurga, the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, around the mid-8th century.
 
• The defeat of Kirtivarman II marked the end of the Chalukya rule and the rise of the Rashtrakutas in the Deccan.
 
• Dantidurga's victory over Kirtivarman II is well-documented in various inscriptions and historical records.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chalukya Dynasty**

 
 
• The Chalukyas were an Indian royal dynasty that ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and the 12th centuries.
 
• Their rule is divided into three distinct but related dynasties: the Badami Chalukyas, the Eastern Chalukyas, and the Western Chalukyas.
 
• They are known for their contribution to art, architecture, and cultural developments in South India.
 
 
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty**
 
 
• The Rashtrakutas were a prominent dynasty that ruled over large parts of the Indian subcontinent between the 6th and 10th centuries.
 
• They are well-known for their patronage of art and architecture, most notably the rock-cut temples of Ellora.
 
• Under their reign, the Deccan region witnessed significant economic, cultural, and political advancements.
 
 
 
• **Dantidurga**
 
 
• Dantidurga was the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty.
 
• He is credited with overthrowing the Chalukyan rule and establishing the Rashtrakuta Empire in the Deccan.
 
• His victory over Kirtivarman II is seen as a significant turning point in the history of South India.
 
 
 
• **Historical Records**
 
 
• Inscriptions and texts from the period provide valuable insights into the political and cultural history of the Deccan region during the time of the Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas.
 
• These records are crucial for understanding the transitions of power and the impact of these dynasties on Indian history.

questions.question: The Early Vedic economy was primarily based on _______ activity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pastoral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Early Vedic economy was primarily based on pastoral activities, focusing on cattle rearing and dairy production.
 
• Cattle were considered a significant measure of wealth and were often used as currency for trade and barter.
 
• The Rigvedic society placed immense importance on cows, and terms like "Gomat" (possessing cows) indicated prosperity.
 
• Pastoralism was central to the Vedic way of life, and cattle played a crucial role in their rituals, social status, and daily subsistence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Early Vedic Literature**

 
 
• The Rigveda, one of the oldest texts, provides detailed insights into the pastoral lifestyle of the Early Vedic people.
 
• Verses in the Rigveda often praise cattle and describe various pastoral activities.
 
 
 
• **Socio-Economic Structure**
 
 
• The society was primarily tribal and kin-based, with clans led by chiefs known as "Rajan."
 
• Wealth was measured in terms of cattle, and social hierarchy often depended on the number of cattle owned.
 
 
 
• **Religious Practices**
 
 
• Many Vedic rituals and sacrifices, such as the Ashvamedha and Rajasuya, involved the use of cattle.
 
• Cows were considered sacred and were central to various religious ceremonies and offerings.
 
 
 
• **Transition to Agriculture**
 
 
• Although the Early Vedic economy was pastoral, there was a gradual shift towards agriculture during the Later Vedic period.
 
• This transition was marked by the settlement of tribes in the fertile plains of the Ganges and Yamuna rivers.

questions.question: Who among the following is the dance guru from Odisha credited with having revived the Odissi dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelucharan Mohapatra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra** is renowned for reviving the classical Indian dance form of Odissi.
 
• He was born on January 8, 1926, in Raghurajpur, Odisha.
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra was awarded the prestigious **Padma Vibhushan** in 2000 for his contributions to Indian classical dance.
 
• He was also a recipient of the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** and the **Kalidas Samman**.
 
• He established the **Srjan** (Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Odissi Nrityabasa) dance school in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, to teach and promote Odissi dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi Dance**

 
 
• Odissi is one of the classical dance forms of India that originated in Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by its fluid movements, intricate gestures, and expressive eyes.
 
• The dance form is traditionally performed as a form of worship to Lord Jagannath.
 
• Odissi has a rich history, with roots tracing back to the ancient temples of Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• This is the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists.
 
• It is awarded by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.
 
• The award consists of a cash prize, a citation, and a tamrapatra (bronze plaque).
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors in India, awarded annually on Republic Day.
 
• They are categorized into three levels: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
• These awards recognize achievements in various disciplines including arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
 
 
• **Kalidas Samman**
 
 
• This is a prestigious arts award presented annually by the government of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is named after the classical Sanskrit writer Kalidasa.
 
• The award is given for outstanding achievements in the fields of classical music, classical dance, theatre, and visual arts.

questions.question: Which of the following awards was conferred upon the Chhau dancer Siba Prasad Das in 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Siba Prasad Das is a renowned Chhau dancer known for his contributions to the traditional dance form.
 
• In 2022, he was conferred with the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award is given to artists who have significantly contributed to the field of performing arts in India.
 
• The award is part of the initiative by Sangeet Natak Akademi to recognize and honor the talent and dedication of artists in various performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**

 
 
• It is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama.
 
• Founded in 1952, it aims to promote and preserve India's vast cultural heritage of performing arts.
 
• The Akademi awards are considered the highest national recognition given to practicing artists.
 
 
 
• **Chhau Dance**
 
 
• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance with martial, tribal, and folk traditions.
 
• It is predominantly performed in the Indian states of Odisha, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.
 
• The dance is recognized by UNESCO as an intangible cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri**
 
 
• It is one of the highest civilian awards in India, awarded for distinguished service in various fields.
 
• The award was instituted in 1954 and is given annually on Republic Day.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship**
 
 
• This is a prestigious fellowship awarded by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to individuals for their lifetime achievement in the field of performing arts.
 
• It is different from the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, which is for significant contributions in a specific period.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are influenced by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhian philosophy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution are primarily inspired by the Gandhian philosophy.
 
• These principles reflect Mahatma Gandhi's vision for a socio-economic framework that aims at ensuring social justice and the welfare of the people.
 
• The DPSPs cover various aspects such as promoting cottage industries, living wages for workers, and the organization of village Panchayats, which are rooted in Gandhian values.
 
• The goal of these principles is to create a just society and to ensure that the state works towards the welfare of all its citizens.
 
• Though not enforceable by law, these principles guide the government in making policies and laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• The DPSPs are included in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• They are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government and are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court.
 
• The aim is to establish a welfare state by securing social, economic, and political justice.
 
 
 
• **Gandhian Principles in DPSP**
 
 
• Promotion of cottage industries in rural areas (Article 43).
 
• Organization of village Panchayats (Article 40).
 
• Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections (Article 46).
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights (Part III) are enforceable by courts, whereas DPSPs are not.
 
• Both aim at the establishment of a just society and are complementary to each other.
 
• While Fundamental Rights ensure political democracy, DPSPs aim at social and economic democracy.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• The concept of DPSPs was borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
 
• The framers of the Indian Constitution were influenced by the Irish nationalist movement and Gandhi's philosophy.
 
• They wanted to ensure that the state would work towards the welfare of all citizens, particularly the marginalized sections of society.

questions.question: Select the correct combination of famous palaces and their locations in Rajasthan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lalgarh Palace – Bikaner**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lalgarh Palace** is located in the city of **Bikaner** in Rajasthan.
 
• The palace was built between 1902 and 1926 for Maharaja Ganga Singh.
 
• It was designed by the British architect Sir Samuel Swinton Jacob.
 
• The palace exhibits a perfect amalgamation of Rajput, Mughal, and European architectural styles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rambagh Palace**

 
 
• Located in Jaipur, it is one of the most famous palaces in Rajasthan.
 
• It was originally built in 1835 and was used as a royal guesthouse and hunting lodge.
 
• It was later converted into a palace and is now a luxury hotel.
 
 
 
• **Umaid Bhawan Palace**
 
 
• Located in Jodhpur, it is one of the world's largest private residences.
 
• The palace was completed in 1943 and is named after Maharaja Umaid Singh.
 
• It is divided into a luxury hotel, a museum, and the residence of the royal family.
 
 
 
• **Taj Lake Palace**
 
 
• Located in Udaipur, it is a luxury hotel situated on Lake Pichola.
 
• The palace was built in 1746 under the direction of Maharana Jagat Singh II.
 
• It is famous for its stunning architecture and picturesque location.
